resolution: User pointed out their wheel well sits on a SLANTED body panel and asked if they should just flatten it. Answered + fixed — no flattening needed. Two-part response: (1) the axle correctly snaps to the dominant cardinal axis so the wheel stays VERTICAL and rolls — a wheel is never tilted to match a slanted fender, exactly like a real car, so the well's slant should NOT tilt the tire; (2) the only thing the slant broke was the RADIUS, which faceWheelFit measured from cardinal in-plane extent (foreshortened by the slant). Fixed faceWheelFit to size the radius from the median 3D distance centroid→rim verts, which is slant-INDEPENDENT and correct for a round well (the well's n-gon cap) at any angle. Center stays the centroid, axle stays the dominant-cardinal snap. Updated wheelMount.test.ts: replaced the in-plane-extent radius assertion with a round-well (hexagon) radius/axle test and added a slant-independence test (a flat vs ~20°-tilted hexagon of the same circumradius size the identical radius). 6/6 pass via esbuild+v8cli; wheelMount.ts transpiles clean. Commit b746467c2. So the user can use slanted wheel wells directly — '⊚ wheel from face' now sizes them right and keeps the tire vertical.
